rules.title: Reinsure only with a company licensed to carry the class
rules.instrument: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (42): The Company may not reinsure with another company unless the other company is licensed to carry out the insurance type entrusted to reinsure it.
rules.requirement: The counterparty must be licensed for the class of business ceded — a UAE licence, or a home-state licence naming the class for a reinsurer abroad. A UAE carrier may reinsure inside or outside the State, but never with an unlicensed company.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز للشركة أن تعيد التأمين لدى شركة أخرى ما لم تكن تلك الشركة مرخصة لمزاولة نوع التأمين المطلوب إعادة تأمينه.

rules.title: A counterparty at or above the rating floor, or board diligence on file
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (18): acceptance of reinsurance business is conditional on the reinsurer meeting the classification stipulated, and business exceeding retention must be covered with reinsurers who have that classification, subject to the stated exceptions.
rules.requirement: A reinsurance counterparty should hold a financial strength rating of BBB (S&P) or equivalent — Baa2 or better — or, if it does not, the placement needs documented board-level due diligence before it is bound.
rules.requirementAr: يُشترط في شركة إعادة التأمين الحصول على تصنيف مالي لا يقل عن BBB أو ما يعادله، وإلا وجب توثيق العناية الواجبة على مستوى مجلس الإدارة.

rules.title: Recoverables count as admissible assets only at or above the floor
rules.instrument: Minimum capital requirement — CBUAE financial regulations — capital, assets and technical provisions
rules.clause: Assets available to meet insurance liabilities may include reinsurance recoverables where the reinsurer is rated BBB or better.
rules.requirement: Money due from a counterparty below the floor is not an admissible asset: the return must show the recoverable without credit for it, and the solvency position must be read with that in mind.
rules.requirementAr: لا تُعد المبالغ المستحقة من معيد تأمين دون التصنيف المطلوب أصولاً مقبولة، ويجب بيانها دون احتساب رصيد لها.

rules.title: Every cession sits inside the board-approved retention and reinsurance plan
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: The company shall prepare a three-year plan concerning retention and reinsurance for each type and class, approve it at the board, and review it annually during the three months before each year, covering retention and treaty limits, treaty types and facultative cessions.
rules.requirement: A cession must be permitted by the plan the board approved, and the plan must have been reviewed inside the year before the placement. A cession outside the plan is refused; a plan whose review window has passed is escalated.
rules.requirementAr: يجب أن تكون إعادة التأمين ضمن الخطة المعتمدة من مجلس الإدارة، وأن تُراجع الخطة سنوياً خلال الأشهر الثلاثة السابقة لكل سنة.
evidence: board minute of the annual review

rules.title: A foreign branch files its head-office reinsurance certificate every year
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: A foreign insurance company operating in the State through a branch shall annually submit a certified certificate from its head office supporting that the business subscribed within the State and exceeding its retention is covered by reinsurance with reinsurers who have the classification stipulated in Article (18).
rules.requirement: Where the counterparty is the branch of a foreign company, its annual certified certificate must be on file and no more than twelve months old.
rules.requirementAr: على فرع شركة التأمين الأجنبية العاملة في الدولة أن يقدم سنوياً شهادة معتمدة من المركز الرئيسي تفيد بأن الأعمال التي تتجاوز حد الاحتفاظ مغطاة لدى معيدي تأمين حاصلين على التصنيف المطلوب.

rules.title: Accepting treaty reinsurance needs approval and capital
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (39): in order to accept the treaty reinsurance business, the insurance company established in the State is required to obtain approval from the Director General, and the minimum subscribed and paid-up capital of the company shall not be less than AED 350,000,000.
rules.requirement: Inward treaty business may only be accepted with the Director General's approval, articles that authorise accepting reinsurance, and at least AED 350,000,000 of subscribed and paid-up capital.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز قبول أعمال إعادة التأمين الاتفاقي إلا بعد الحصول على موافقة المدير العام، وبألا يقل رأس المال المكتتب المدفوع عن 350,000,000 درهم.

rules.title: Facultative acceptance only within retention or under a treaty
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (38): the accepted liabilities shall be either within the company's retention or exceeding it, in which case the company must have a reinsurance treaty that protects the surplus and contains a provision allowing it to accept facultative reinsurance within determined limits; re-ceding that surplus facultatively needs the prior approval of the ceding company.
rules.requirement: Facultative business may be accepted only inside the retention or under a treaty that protects the surplus and permits facultative acceptance; passing the surplus on needs the ceding company's prior approval.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز قبول أعمال إعادة التأمين الاختياري إلا في حدود حد الاحتفاظ أو في وجود اتفاقية تحمي الفائض وتجيز القبول، مع الحصول على موافقة مسبقة من الشركة المتنازلة عند إعادة التنازل.

rules.title: A tender is only offered with a leading reinsurer behind the surplus
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (31): the company shall obtain approval, before submitting its offer, from a leading reinsurer that meets the conditions stipulated in Article (18), where the tender's cover is one for which the company has no reinsurance treaty covering the surplus above its retention.
rules.requirement: Where a tender is not covered by treaty, written approval from a leading reinsurer that meets the classification requirement must be on file before the offer goes in.
rules.requirementAr: يجب الحصول على موافقة من معيد تأمين رائد يستوفي شروط المادة (18) قبل تقديم العرض إذا لم تكن تغطية المناقصة مشمولة باتفاقية إعادة تأمين.

rules.title: Participant risk money goes to retakaful only
rules.instrument: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (42), read with the takaful regulations: the class entrusted must be carried by the counterparty, and a takaful operator's participant risk fund may only be protected by retakaful.
rules.requirement: A takaful window cedes only to a retakaful operator or a Shariah-compliant retakaful window. Participant risk money never enters a conventional pool — a breach is refused at the register, not corrected afterwards.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز لصندوق مخاطر المشتركين في شركة تكافل أن يعيد التأمين إلا لدى معيد تكافل، ولا يجوز تحويل أموال المخاطر للمشتركين إلى صندوق تقليدي.

rules.title: A free-zone company reinsures, and does nothing else outside the zone
rules.instrument: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (64): insurance companies licensed to operate in the financial free zones may not carry out any activity outside such zones in the State, except for reinsurance.
rules.requirement: A free-zone counterparty is a permitted reinsurer: the placement may stand, and the decision records the limit on what that company may do outside its zone.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز لشركات التأمين المرخصة في المناطق المالية الحرة مزاولة أي نشاط خارج تلك المناطق داخل الدولة، باستثناء إعادة التأمين.

rules.title: A foreign branch lodges the bank guarantee its licence requires
rules.instrument: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (50): the foreign insurance company's branch shall submit an irrevocable bank guarantee in favour of the CBUAE of not less than AED 100,000,000 where it carries on insurance activity, and not less than AED 250,000,000 where it carries on reinsurance activity.
rules.requirement: Where the counterparty is a foreign branch writing reinsurance, an irrevocable bank guarantee of at least AED 250,000,000 (AED 100,000,000 for insurance) must be lodged with the CBUAE.

body.limitation: the store lives with the process: the registers themselves are what a restart restores, and this log is the running proof that nothing they reported was dropped

outbox.detail: 18 record(s) chained from the beginning: nothing dropped, nothing reordered, nothing edited

body.limitation: The registers are sealed into a canonical, checksummed snapshot with a migration path and replayed into a fresh world on restore; the outbox proves nothing was dropped between snapshots; every record remembers how far the books had got when it was made and is re-proved against the books of its own moment; and the registers carry the actions they took, so a restart puts them back by taking those actions again, checked journal for journal. Two limits are stated rather than papered over: it is not yet a database (no transactional write, no concurrent-reader isolation, no incremental streaming of the outbox), and an action that posts no journal — a cash call, a free reinstatement — is anchored by the number of journals the books held when it happened, which places it in the right window but cannot order two such actions that land inside the same journal.

rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (42): The Company may not reinsure with another company unless the other company is licensed to carry out the insurance type entrusted to reinsure it.
rules.requirement: The counterparty must be licensed for the class of business ceded — a UAE licence, or a home-state licence naming the class for a reinsurer abroad. A UAE carrier may reinsure inside or outside the State, but never with an unlicensed company.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز للشركة أن تعيد التأمين لدى شركة أخرى ما لم تكن تلك الشركة مرخصة لمزاولة نوع التأمين المطلوب إعادة تأمينه.

rules.title: A counterparty at or above the rating floor, or board diligence on file
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (18): acceptance of reinsurance business is conditional on the reinsurer meeting the classification stipulated, and business exceeding retention must be covered with reinsurers who have that classification, subject to the stated exceptions.
rules.requirement: A reinsurance counterparty should hold a financial strength rating of BBB (S&P) or equivalent — Baa2 or better — or, if it does not, the placement needs documented board-level due diligence before it is bound.
rules.requirementAr: يُشترط في شركة إعادة التأمين الحصول على تصنيف مالي لا يقل عن BBB أو ما يعادله، وإلا وجب توثيق العناية الواجبة على مستوى مجلس الإدارة.

rules.title: Recoverables count as admissible assets only at or above the floor
rules.instrument: Minimum capital requirement — CBUAE financial regulations — capital, assets and technical provisions
rules.clause: Assets available to meet insurance liabilities may include reinsurance recoverables where the reinsurer is rated BBB or better.
rules.requirement: Money due from a counterparty below the floor is not an admissible asset: the return must show the recoverable without credit for it, and the solvency position must be read with that in mind.
rules.requirementAr: لا تُعد المبالغ المستحقة من معيد تأمين دون التصنيف المطلوب أصولاً مقبولة، ويجب بيانها دون احتساب رصيد لها.

rules.title: Every cession sits inside the board-approved retention and reinsurance plan
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: The company shall prepare a three-year plan concerning retention and reinsurance for each type and class, approve it at the board, and review it annually during the three months before each year, covering retention and treaty limits, treaty types and facultative cessions.
rules.requirement: A cession must be permitted by the plan the board approved, and the plan must have been reviewed inside the year before the placement. A cession outside the plan is refused; a plan whose review window has passed is escalated.
rules.requirementAr: يجب أن تكون إعادة التأمين ضمن الخطة المعتمدة من مجلس الإدارة، وأن تُراجع الخطة سنوياً خلال الأشهر الثلاثة السابقة لكل سنة.
evidence: board minute of the annual review

rules.title: A foreign branch files its head-office reinsurance certificate every year
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: A foreign insurance company operating in the State through a branch shall annually submit a certified certificate from its head office supporting that the business subscribed within the State and exceeding its retention is covered by reinsurance with reinsurers who have the classification stipulated in Article (18).
rules.requirement: Where the counterparty is the branch of a foreign company, its annual certified certificate must be on file and no more than twelve months old.
rules.requirementAr: على فرع شركة التأمين الأجنبية العاملة في الدولة أن يقدم سنوياً شهادة معتمدة من المركز الرئيسي تفيد بأن الأعمال التي تتجاوز حد الاحتفاظ مغطاة لدى معيدي تأمين حاصلين على التصنيف المطلوب.

rules.title: Accepting treaty reinsurance needs approval and capital
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (39): in order to accept the treaty reinsurance business, the insurance company established in the State is required to obtain approval from the Director General, and the minimum subscribed and paid-up capital of the company shall not be less than AED 350,000,000.
rules.requirement: Inward treaty business may only be accepted with the Director General's approval, articles that authorise accepting reinsurance, and at least AED 350,000,000 of subscribed and paid-up capital.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز قبول أعمال إعادة التأمين الاتفاقي إلا بعد الحصول على موافقة المدير العام، وبألا يقل رأس المال المكتتب المدفوع عن 350,000,000 درهم.

rules.title: Facultative acceptance only within retention or under a treaty
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (38): the accepted liabilities shall be either within the company's retention or exceeding it, in which case the company must have a reinsurance treaty that protects the surplus and contains a provision allowing it to accept facultative reinsurance within determined limits; re-ceding that surplus facultatively needs the prior approval of the ceding company.
rules.requirement: Facultative business may be accepted only inside the retention or under a treaty that protects the surplus and permits facultative acceptance; passing the surplus on needs the ceding company's prior approval.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز قبول أعمال إعادة التأمين الاختياري إلا في حدود حد الاحتفاظ أو في وجود اتفاقية تحمي الفائض وتجيز القبول، مع الحصول على موافقة مسبقة من الشركة المتنازلة عند إعادة التنازل.

rules.title: A tender is only offered with a leading reinsurer behind the surplus
rules.instrument: Article (18) — CBUAE reinsurance regulations (Insurance Authority Board Decision No. 23 of 2019, carried into the CBUAE rulebook)
rules.note: Article (18) sets the classification requirement for reinsurers; Articles (31), (38) and (39) are cited by the rules that use them
rules.clause: Article (31): the company shall obtain approval, before submitting its offer, from a leading reinsurer that meets the conditions stipulated in Article (18), where the tender's cover is one for which the company has no reinsurance treaty covering the surplus above its retention.
rules.requirement: Where a tender is not covered by treaty, written approval from a leading reinsurer that meets the classification requirement must be on file before the offer goes in.
rules.requirementAr: يجب الحصول على موافقة من معيد تأمين رائد يستوفي شروط المادة (18) قبل تقديم العرض إذا لم تكن تغطية المناقصة مشمولة باتفاقية إعادة تأمين.

rules.title: Participant risk money goes to retakaful only
rules.instrument: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (42), read with the takaful regulations: the class entrusted must be carried by the counterparty, and a takaful operator's participant risk fund may only be protected by retakaful.
rules.requirement: A takaful window cedes only to a retakaful operator or a Shariah-compliant retakaful window. Participant risk money never enters a conventional pool — a breach is refused at the register, not corrected afterwards.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز لصندوق مخاطر المشتركين في شركة تكافل أن يعيد التأمين إلا لدى معيد تكافل، ولا يجوز تحويل أموال المخاطر للمشتركين إلى صندوق تقليدي.

rules.title: A free-zone company reinsures, and does nothing else outside the zone
rules.instrument: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (64): insurance companies licensed to operate in the financial free zones may not carry out any activity outside such zones in the State, except for reinsurance.
rules.requirement: A free-zone counterparty is a permitted reinsurer: the placement may stand, and the decision records the limit on what that company may do outside its zone.
rules.requirementAr: لا يجوز لشركات التأمين المرخصة في المناطق المالية الحرة مزاولة أي نشاط خارج تلك المناطق داخل الدولة، باستثناء إعادة التأمين.

rules.title: A foreign branch lodges the bank guarantee its licence requires
rules.instrument: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
rules.note: replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 from 16 September 2025, with a transition to 16 September 2026
rules.clause: Article (50): the foreign insurance company's branch shall submit an irrevocable bank guarantee in favour of the CBUAE of not less than AED 100,000,000 where it carries on insurance activity, and not less than AED 250,000,000 where it carries on reinsurance activity.
rules.requirement: Where the counterparty is a foreign branch writing reinsurance, an irrevocable bank guarantee of at least AED 250,000,000 (AED 100,000,000 for insurance) must be lodged with the CBUAE.
rules.requirementAr: يقدم فرع شركة التأمين الأجنبية ضماناً مصرفياً غير قابل للإلغاء لصالح المصرف المركزي لا يقل عن 100,000,000 درهم لمزاولة التأمين و250,000,000 درهم لمزاولة إعادة التأمين.

rules.title: UAE risk insured at home, protected anywhere
rules.instrument: Article (82) — Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 on the Central Bank, the Regulation of Financial Institutions and Activities, and Insurance Business
rules.note: consolidates the insurance law into the CBUAE mandate; the reinsurance freedoms and controls of the 2023 law are carried forward
rules.clause: Article (82)(2): a UAE insurer may reinsure its business with reinsurers located in the UAE or outside the State; a policy may not be concluded with a company outside the State to cover money or property within the State.
rules.requirement: The risk stays with a licensed UAE carrier and the reinsurance may be placed anywhere — the decision records which of the two this placement is.
rules.requirementAr: يجوز لشركة التأمين في الدولة إعادة تأمين أعمالها لدى معيدي تأمين داخل الدولة أو خارجها، دون جواز إبرام وثيقة لدى شركة خارج الدولة لتغطية أموال أو ممتلكات داخل الدولة.

findings.requirement: A takaful window cedes only to a retakaful operator or a Shariah-compliant retakaful window. Participant risk money never enters a conventional pool — a breach is refused at the register, not corrected afterwards.

findings.title: Reinsure only with a company licensed to carry the class
findings.detail: Oriana Re (unlicensed) holds no licence to carry the class ceded — a policy placed on an unlicensed company is void, so this placement cannot stand
findings.clause: Article (42) — Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 Regulating Insurance Activities
findings.requirement: The counterparty must be licensed for the class of business ceded — a UAE licence, or a home-state licence naming the class for a reinsurer abroad. A UAE carrier may reinsure inside or outside the State, but never with an unlicensed company.
findings.requirementAr: لا يجوز للشركة أن تعيد التأمين لدى شركة أخرى ما لم تكن تلك الشركة مرخصة لمزاولة نوع التأمين المطلوب إعادة تأمينه.

findings.requirement: A reinsurance counterparty should hold a financial strength rating of BBB (S&P) or equivalent — Baa2 or better — or, if it does not, the placement needs documented board-level due diligence before it is bound.
findings.requirementAr: يُشترط في شركة إعادة التأمين الحصول على تصنيف مالي لا يقل عن BBB أو ما يعادله، وإلا وجب توثيق العناية الواجبة على مستوى مجلس الإدارة.

findings.clause: Minimum capital requirement — CBUAE financial regulations — capital, assets and technical provisions
findings.requirement: Money due from a counterparty below the floor is not an admissible asset: the return must show the recoverable without credit for it, and the solvency position must be read with that in mind.
findings.requirementAr: لا تُعد المبالغ المستحقة من معيد تأمين دون التصنيف المطلوب أصولاً مقبولة، ويجب بيانها دون احتساب رصيد لها.

findings.requirement: A cession must be permitted by the plan the board approved, and the plan must have been reviewed inside the year before the placement. A cession outside the plan is refused; a plan whose review window has passed is escalated.

products.name: Whole of Life Protection

products.name: Joint Life Term Cover
products.blurb: One sum assured over two lives, payable on the first death (or the second, if elected at issue).

products.name: Family Term Takaful
products.blurb: Pure protection takaful: the whole contribution less wakalah fee goes to the participant risk fund as tabarru’.

products.name: Capital-Back Endowment Plan
products.blurb: A savings contract that returns the sum assured at maturity, with survival benefits paid at intervals along the way.

products.name: Children’s Education Endowment
products.blurb: A fund built to a child’s university dates, with a waiver so the plan completes even if the paying parent dies.

products.name: Retirement Endowment with Profits
products.blurb: A with-profits endowment that converts to an annuity or pays a lump sum at the elected retirement date.

products.name: Five-Year Short Endowment
products.blurb: A five-year savings contract with a single or regular premium and a guaranteed maturity value.

products.name: Money-Back Endowment Plan
products.blurb: A proportion of the sum assured is paid at each survival interval, the balance with bonuses at maturity.

products.name: Unit-Linked Wealth Endowment
products.blurb: An endowment whose maturity value is the fund: units allocated at each dealing point, with a minimum death benefit guaranteed.

products.name: Takaful Education Savings Plan
products.blurb: A Shariah-compliant education fund built in the participant investment fund, with tabarru’ cover on the paying parent.

products.name: Standalone Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: A lump sum on first diagnosis of a condition on the filed schedule, independent of any life cover.

products.name: Comprehensive Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: The widest filed condition schedule, including major organ failure, stroke and coronary artery bypass.

products.name: Early-Stage Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: Pays a proportion of the sum assured at an early stage of a listed condition, and again at an advanced stage.

products.name: Multi-Pay Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: Pays once per condition group up to a stated number of claims, with a survival period between them.

products.name: Women’s Specific Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: Conditions specific to women, including the listed gynaecological cancers and complications of pregnancy.

products.name: Children’s Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: A lump sum on a child’s diagnosis, with a parental accommodation benefit while the child is hospitalised.

products.name: Term Life with Critical Illness Bundle
products.blurb: Level term life with critical illness cover attached as a rider, priced as one contract and one premium.

products.name: Critical Illness Takaful
products.blurb: Wakalah-based critical illness cover out of the participant risk fund, with a Shariah-compliant condition schedule.

products.name: Lifestyle Income Protection
products.blurb: A monthly benefit after a deferred period when illness or injury stops the customer working, to a stated retirement age.

products.name: Lifestyle Loan Protection
products.blurb: Services a named personal loan while the customer cannot work, up to the outstanding balance and a monthly cap.

products.name: Lifestyle Protection Plan
products.blurb: One plan carrying death, critical illness and income replacement, so a household is covered on all three axes.

products.name: Lifestyle Wealth Plan (Unit-Linked)
products.blurb: A lifestyle plan whose savings leg is invested in units, with the protection leg charged per mille from the fund.

products.name: Lifestyle Takaful Plan
products.blurb: A wakalah family takaful plan combining savings in the participant investment fund with tabarru’ protection.

products.name: Mortgage Redemption Plan
products.blurb: A decreasing sum assured matched to the lender’s amortisation schedule, assigned to the bank at issue.

products.name: Mortgage Protection (Level)
products.blurb: A level sum assured over the mortgage term for a customer on an interest-only or bullet facility.

products.name: Mortgage Protection with Critical Illness
products.blurb: Mortgage protection that also clears the loan on a listed diagnosis, not only on death.

products.name: Mortgage Payment Protection
products.blurb: Pays the mortgage instalment for a limited number of months after involuntary unemployment, illness or accident.

products.name: Mortgage Takaful Plan
products.blurb: A decreasing takaful cover over a Shariah-compliant home finance facility, assigned to the financier.

products.name: Individual Inpatient Medical
products.blurb: Hospital admission, surgery and day-case treatment on the network, with a stated room category.

products.name: Outpatient & Inpatient Medical
products.blurb: Inpatient cover plus consultations, diagnostics and pharmacy on the outpatient side, subject to a co-pay.

products.name: Maternity & Newborn Cover
products.blurb: Antenatal care, delivery and newborn care, with a waiting period before the first claim is payable.

products.name: Dental & Optical Care Plan
products.blurb: Routine and major dental treatment plus optical correction, on an annual limit per discipline.

products.name: International Medical with Evacuation
products.blurb: Worldwide treatment including medical evacuation and repatriation, for a customer who travels or is posted abroad.

products.name: SME Group Medical Scheme
products.blurb: A staff medical scheme for a small employer, rated on the group’s age profile rather than individual evidence.

products.name: Corporate Group Medical Scheme
products.blurb: A large-group scheme with a network tier per employee grade, experience-rated at renewal.

products.name: Health Takaful Plan
products.blurb: A wakalah health plan with claims paid from the participant risk fund and surplus shared back under the filed gates.

products.name: Comprehensive Motor Cover
products.blurb: Own-damage and third-party cover for a private vehicle, with agency repair for the first years.

products.name: Third-Party Liability Motor
products.blurb: The statutory minimum: third-party bodily injury and property damage, with no own-damage cover.

products.name: Commercial Fleet Motor
products.blurb: A whole fleet on one policy and one renewal date, rated on the schedule of vehicles and the claims history.

products.name: Single-Trip Travel Cover
products.blurb: Emergency medical, repatriation, cancellation and baggage for one journey, from the day of departure.

products.name: Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
products.blurb: Unlimited trips inside a twelve-month period, each up to a stated number of days.

products.name: Schengen Visa Travel Cover
products.blurb: The minimum medical and repatriation limit a Schengen visa application requires, with the certificate issued at once.

products.name: Family Travel Cover
products.blurb: One policy for two adults and their dependent children travelling together, at a family rate.

products.name: Senior Traveller Cover
products.blurb: Travel cover for the over-65s with a declared-condition questionnaire and a higher medical limit.

products.name: Business Travel & Accident Cover
products.blurb: Corporate travel with accident benefits, equipment cover and a political-evacuation extension.

products.name: Travel Takaful Plan
products.blurb: A short-period travel takaful certificate with the contribution treated as tabarru’ into the participant risk fund.

products.name: Personal Accident Cover
products.blurb: Accidental death and permanent disablement on a scheduled scale, with a weekly indemnity while off work.

products.name: Executive Personal Accident
products.blurb: Worldwide 24-hour accident cover for a named executive, with medical expenses and repatriation included.

products.name: Fidelity Guarantee
products.blurb: Direct financial loss from an employee’s dishonesty, named or on a blanket basis with a per-claim limit.

products.name: Money Insurance
products.blurb: Cash in transit and cash in safe, with an infidelity extension for a named custodian.

products.name: Plate Glass Cover
products.blurb: Shopfront and signage glass on an all-risks basis, including the cost of temporary boarding up.

products.name: Cyber & Data Breach Cover
products.blurb: First-party incident response and business interruption, plus third-party liability for a data breach.

products.name: Fire & Perils Commercial Property
products.blurb: Buildings, plant and stock against fire and the named perils, at reinstatement or indemnity value as elected.

products.name: Property All-Risks Cover
products.blurb: All-risks cover on scheduled property, with the standard exclusions and a per-item limit.

products.name: Burglary & Housebreaking Cover
products.blurb: Stock and contents lost to forcible and violent entry, with a warranty on the alarm and locks.

products.name: Public Liability
products.blurb: Legal liability to third parties for bodily injury and property damage arising from the business.

products.name: Employer’s Liability
products.blurb: Liability for an employee’s injury or disease arising out of employment, to the statutory limit.

products.name: Professional Indemnity
products.blurb: Negligent advice, design or supervision, on a claims-made basis with a stated retroactive date.

products.name: Product Liability
products.blurb: Liability for injury or damage caused by a product supplied, with a recall extension available.

products.name: Directors & Officers Liability
products.blurb: Defence costs and damages for a wrongful act by a director or officer, with entity cover for securities claims.

products.name: Contractors’ All Risk
products.blurb: The works, temporary works and materials on a construction site, with a maintenance period extension.

products.name: Erection All Risk
products.blurb: Machinery and steelwork during erection, testing and commissioning, including the cost of re-erection.

products.name: Machinery Breakdown
products.blurb: Sudden and unforeseen physical damage to plant, with consequential loss available as an extension.

products.name: Boiler & Pressure Vessel Cover
products.blurb: Inspection and explosion cover on boilers and pressure vessels, tied to the statutory inspection cycle.

products.name: Marine Cargo — Single Voyage
products.blurb: One consignment on one voyage, on Institute Cargo Clauses A, B or C as elected.

products.name: Marine Cargo — Annual Open Cover
products.blurb: All shipments declared under an annual contract, with a per-conveyance limit and monthly bordereaux.

products.name: Air Cargo Cover
products.blurb: Airfreight consignments on Institute Cargo Clauses (Air), including warehouse-to-warehouse transit.

products.name: Land Transit Cargo Cover
products.blurb: Road and rail transit inside the country and across borders, with a conveyance warranty.

products.name: Cargo Storage Cover
products.blurb: Goods held in a warehouse or free zone between transits, on a stock-declaration basis.

products.name: Terminal Operators’ Liability
products.blurb: Legal liability of a terminal or stevedore for cargo in its care, custody and control.

products.name: Marine Cargo Takaful
products.blurb: Cargo cover written as takaful, with claims met from the participant risk fund and a wakalah fee to the operator.

products.name: Marine Hull & Machinery
products.blurb: The vessel itself, her machinery and equipment, on Institute Hull Clauses with a named deductible.

products.name: Hull War Risks
products.blurb: War, strikes and related perils on the hull, written separately from the hull policy and cancellable at short notice.

products.name: Yacht & Pleasure Craft Hull
products.blurb: Hull, machinery and third-party liability for a pleasure craft, with a navigation warranty.

products.name: Aircraft Hull Cover
products.blurb: Hull and spares for a fixed-wing or rotary aircraft, with a pilot-warranty and a grounded-risk option.

products.name: Protection & Indemnity (P&I)
products.blurb: A shipowner’s liability to crew, passengers, cargo interests and the environment, including wreck removal.

products.name: Offshore Energy Hull Cover
products.blurb: Mobile offshore units, jack-ups and support vessels, with a well-control extension available.

products.name: Home Contents Cover
products.blurb: Household contents against fire, theft, water damage and the named perils, with a single-article limit.

products.name: Homeowner’s Comprehensive Cover
products.blurb: The building and its contents on one policy, with alternative accommodation while the home is uninhabitable.

products.name: Renter’s Contents Cover
products.blurb: Contents cover for a tenant, with tenant’s liability for damage to the landlord’s property.

products.name: Landlord Building Cover
products.blurb: A let property’s building and the landlord’s liability, with a loss-of-rent extension.

products.name: Valuables & Jewellery All-Risk
products.blurb: Scheduled jewellery, watches and art on an all-risks basis, with a valuation certificate required per item.

products.name: Home Emergency Assistance
products.blurb: Call-out and repair for a plumbing, electrical or air-conditioning failure, on an annual limit per trade.

products.name: Home Takaful Plan
products.blurb: Building and contents cover written as takaful, with the contribution split between tabarru’ and wakalah fee.

products.name: Group Term Life Scheme
products.blurb: A free-cover limit per member with a scheme rate on the group’s age profile, and a dependent option.

products.name: Group Personal Accident Scheme
products.blurb: Accident benefits for a defined employee group, rated flat per head with no individual evidence.

products.name: Group Critical Illness Scheme
products.blurb: A uniform critical illness sum assured for every member of the group, paid on first diagnosis.

products.name: Group Family Takaful Scheme
products.blurb: An employee takaful scheme: contributions are tabarru’ into a scheme-specific participant risk fund.

# Rate sample template — 3 product(s), amounts in AED.
# Fill the rows in, keep the headers, delete these # lines if you like — the importer skips them.
# Age from / Age to are inclusive entry ages. Sum assured to is exclusive; leave it blank for "and above".
# Occupation class: blank or 0 = every class; 1-5 = that rank only (1 professional … 5 underground/offshore).
# Gender: male, female or unisex. A male or female row beats a unisex row when both match.
# Rate type: "premium" is the annual rate per 1,000 of sum assured; "mortality" is the unit-linked
#   cost of insurance per 1,000 of sum assured per month, and it is what an illustration is sensitive to.
# Channel / Partner: leave blank for the base tariff. A partner row must name its channel.
# Two rows with the same product, type, gender, ages, class, sum band, channel and partner are the same
#   row: the upload replaces it rather than adding a second one, so re-running a file is safe.

rules.branch: A provider may only sell through a country in which it holds a registered, licensed branch.
rules.licence: The branch licence and the provider permission must both cover the product book being sold.
rules.reinsurance: Every provider/country pair needs its own reinsurance arrangement; Takaful business needs retakaful.
rules.currency: The product filing, the branch and the channel-country presence must all be in the country’s own currency.
rules.permission: Conventional and Takaful are separate permissions at channel, sub-channel and partner level; the effective permission is the narrowest of the three.
rules.money: Premium is managed by the local branch and the investment is held in the country where the quotation was generated.

example.description: Marsh Broker (call centre: conventional + Takaful; agency desk: conventional only) selling three carriers in the UAE, the UK and Singapore, each in its own currency, with a registered branch and a country reinsurance arrangement per carrier.

options.label: Age Nearest Birthday (ANB — 6-month / half-year rule)
options.summary: Rounds to the closest birthday on the valuation date: adds 1 year once 6 months (or half the birthday year) have elapsed.

options.label: Age Next Birthday (ANxB — upcoming birthday age)
options.summary: Uses the age attained on the upcoming birthday (completed years + 1, or completed years if valued on the exact birthday).

options.label: Age Last Birthday (ALB — completed integer years)
options.summary: Uses exact completed years since date of birth as of the valuation date, with no upward rounding.

stages.title: Customer onboarding & identity verification
stages.purpose: Create the golden record from a verified identity document, in both languages, with the customer’s consent to process their data.
stages.regulatoryBasis: KYC / CBUAE customer identification: a verified identity document and a recorded consent before any sale.

stages.title: Customer 360 profile, consent & duplicate check
stages.purpose: Confirm the contact details, capture the consent scopes actually needed, check the register for a duplicate of this human being, and record tax residence.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Data-protection and FATCA/CRS: purpose-limited consent, in-country residency of customer data, and tax residence on file.

fields.label: Why the match is not the same customer
fields.defaultLabel: Why the match is not the same customer

fields.label: Consent scopes granted
fields.hint: e.g. customer.exists, customer.name, customer.contact, customer.holdings, marketing

fields.label: Where this customer’s data is processed
fields.defaultLabel: Where this customer’s data is processed

stages.title: Needs-analysis questionnaire
stages.purpose: Ask the questions the country’s pack requires, and derive the protection gap and the premium the customer can actually afford.
stages.regulatoryBasis: AE and MY packs: no life, medical, unit-linked or travel sale before a documented needs analysis with an identifier.

fields.label: Country whose pack governs this sale
fields.defaultLabel: Country whose pack governs this sale

fields.label: Questionnaire answers

fields.label: Customer agrees to the needs-analysis attestation
fields.defaultLabel: Customer agrees to the needs-analysis attestation

stages.title: Product / item recommendation list
stages.purpose: Rank the catalogue against the evaluated need, show the customer the alternatives on the same axes, and record which product they chose.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Suitability and comparison disclosure: the recommendation must answer the stated objective and the alternatives must be presented.

fields.label: Product selected from the recommendation list
fields.defaultLabel: Product selected from the recommendation list

fields.label: Alternative products were presented and discussed
fields.defaultLabel: Alternative products were presented and discussed

fields.label: Why this product answers the need

stages.title: Coverage & premium calculation
stages.purpose: Set the sum assured, term and payment frequency, price the standard premium from the rate table, and test it against what the customer can afford.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Illustration rules and financial underwriting: the sum assured is capped by income, and the premium must sit inside the affordability ceiling.
produces: Standard premium from the rate table

fields.label: Premium paying term (years)
fields.hint: how many years the customer pays for; blank = for the whole benefit term

fields.label: Sold through (omni-channel)

stages.title: Occupational & medical loadings
stages.purpose: Apply the occupational debit and every medical, build, pursuit and family-history loading from the manual, itemised in basis points and money.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Underwriting manual: a loaded premium must be itemised, and any loading given away must carry a named authoriser.

fields.label: Declared medical conditions
fields.hint: Codes from the medical manual, e.g. diabetes-type-2, hypertension-controlled

fields.label: Hazardous pursuits
fields.hint: e.g. scuba-diving, motor-racing, mountaineering-above-6000m

fields.label: Family history
fields.hint: e.g. early-cardiac-death, early-cancer-death

fields.defaultLabel: Customer told about the loading and the exclusions

stages.purpose: Attach the riders the need calls for, price each one, and record the authority for any rider attached without its loading.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Product terms and underwriting authority: a waiver of loading is a decision with a name against it.

fields.label: Riders considered with the customer
fields.hint: Recording "none needed" is a decision; leaving the section blank is not.

fields.label: Riders attached

fields.defaultLabel: Customer accepts the rider terms and their cost

stages.title: Medical requirements
stages.purpose: Work out what this risk has to prove, order it, receive it, and have a human review it — or record a named waiver.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Evidence bands in the product manual: no acceptance without the evidence the band requires, unless a person waives it in writing.

fields.label: Requirements ordered from the customer / clinic
fields.defaultLabel: Requirements ordered from the customer / clinic

fields.label: Results received
fields.hint: One entry per requirement: label, status (ordered/received/reviewed/waived), date, reviewer

stages.title: Fund investment selection & allocation
stages.purpose: Choose the funds and their weights from the live NAV list, split the first contribution exactly, and test the mix against the customer’s risk appetite.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Unit-linked disclosure: the allocation the customer signs is the allocation that is invested, and a Shariah arrangement may only hold screened funds.
produces: Units to be allocated at the next valuation

fields.label: Fund weights
fields.hint: Fund id and percentage; the weights must total exactly 100%

fields.label: Customer acknowledges where the mix sits against their stated appetite
fields.defaultLabel: Customer acknowledges where the mix sits against their stated appetite

fields.label: Customer told which valuation date the units will be bought at
fields.defaultLabel: Customer told which valuation date the units will be bought at

stages.purpose: Record who receives the proceeds and in what shares, with a guardian for any minor, and confirm the designation with the customer.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Policy terms: primary shares must total 100%, and a claim to a minor without a guardian cannot be settled.

fields.label: Beneficiaries and shares
fields.hint: Name, relationship, share %, primary or contingent, date of birth, guardian for a minor

stages.title: Underwriting & medical questionnaire review
stages.purpose: Review and update the medical questionnaire against the evidence on file, then take the underwriting decision under the right authority.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Authority matrix: an AI agent may accept or rate inside its limit and may never decline; declines and over-limit cases go to a named human.

fields.label: Medical questionnaire reviewed against the evidence
fields.defaultLabel: Medical questionnaire reviewed against the evidence

fields.label: Decision taken by an AI agent inside its straight-through limit
fields.defaultLabel: Decision taken by an AI agent inside its straight-through limit

stages.title: Quotation generation (PDF) & email to customer
stages.purpose: Assemble the quotation document with its itemised loadings, riders, allocation and mandated wording, write it as a PDF, and send it to the customer.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Disclosure: the customer must receive the terms, the illustration wording and the free-look period before paying.

fields.label: Email the PDF to the customer
fields.defaultLabel: Email the PDF to the customer

stages.title: Customer review, cooling-off & sign-off
stages.purpose: Give the customer the free-look position in writing, take their signature inside the validity window, and hand the case to buy-online.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Free-look: the cooling-off period must be disclosed and the acceptance must fall inside the quotation’s validity.

stages.title: Buy online — payment options & capture
stages.purpose: Take the first payment by whichever of the six methods the customer chooses, prove it, and reconcile it against the amount due.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Money-in controls: no policy is issued on an uncleared transfer, card data is never stored, and a BNPL provider fee is disclosed.
produces: Handling cost and net to insurer

fields.label: Card number
fields.hint: Validated and reduced to its last four digits; never stored.

stages.title: Underwriting route & binding authority
stages.purpose: Decide who binds the risk: straight through, an in-house underwriter, a senior signature, a freelance underwriter hired to meet the promise, or the reinsurer’s underwriter first.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Binding authority and reinsurance: a case at or above the facultative threshold is offered to the reinsurer before issue, not after.

fields.label: Freelance underwriter engaged for this case
fields.defaultLabel: Freelance underwriter engaged for this case

fields.label: Treaty the risk is offered under
fields.defaultLabel: Treaty the risk is offered under

stages.title: Policy conversion & issuance
stages.purpose: Turn the decided proposal into a policy, receipt the first payment into the chosen funds, and allocate the units at the published valuation.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Issue controls: a policy may only be created on an accepted decision with cleared money and a signed allocation.
produces: Units allocated at the dealing valuation

fields.label: Convert the proposal into a policy
fields.defaultLabel: Convert the proposal into a policy

fields.label: Fund the first contribution is invested in
fields.defaultLabel: Fund the first contribution is invested in

stages.title: Funds allocation & management in force
stages.purpose: Keep the invested mix where the customer signed it: measure drift against the target weights, and rebalance, switch or top up when it moves.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Stewardship and dealing rules: changes are priced at the published valuation on the dealing day the instruction falls in.

fields.label: Allocation reviewed against the signed targets
fields.defaultLabel: Allocation reviewed against the signed targets

fields.label: What was done, or why nothing was needed
fields.defaultLabel: What was done, or why nothing was needed

stages.title: Investment allocations & progress
stages.purpose: Show the customer what their money did: contributions, current value, gain or loss, drift, and the date of the next review.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Illustration honesty: progress is measured at published valuations with the disclaimer that values may fall as well as rise.

stages.title: Servicing: alterations & claims
stages.purpose: Hand the policy to servicing: what may be altered without a financial review, what needs one, and how a claim is registered and decided.
stages.regulatoryBasis: Policy administration: every alteration and claim decision is auditable, with the reason and the authority recorded.

products.name: Global Unit-Linked Plan
products.blurb: Regular-premium unit-linked plan invested across the global growth and balanced funds, with life cover charged per mille each month.

products.name: Level Term Life Protection
products.blurb: A level sum assured for a fixed term: the sum assured does not fall and neither does the premium.

products.name: Comprehensive Medical Cover
products.blurb: Inpatient and outpatient treatment on a recognised network, with pre-authorisation for elective procedures.

products.name: Family Takaful Protection & Savings Plan
products.blurb: Wakalah-based family takaful: part of each contribution is tabarru’ into the participant risk fund, the rest is invested in the Shariah-screened equity fund.

products.name: Pay-as-you-drive Motor Cover
products.blurb: Micro-duration motor cover billed by the day and by the kilometre, charged only between an explicit start and stop.

products.name: Decreasing Term Assurance
products.blurb: A sum assured that falls on a capital-repayment schedule, priced for a customer covering an amortising loan.

products.name: Index-Linked Increasing Term
products.blurb: A sum assured that rises each year with a published index, so the cover keeps pace with the cost of living.

products.name: Convertible Term Assurance
products.blurb: Level term carrying a contractual right to convert to a whole-life or endowment plan without fresh medical evidence.

products.name: Whole of Life Protection
products.blurb: Cover that pays whenever death occurs, with a reviewable premium after the guaranteed period.

products.name: Joint Life Term Cover
products.blurb: One sum assured over two lives, payable on the first death (or the second, if elected at issue).

products.name: Family Term Takaful
products.blurb: Pure protection takaful: the whole contribution less wakalah fee goes to the participant risk fund as tabarru’.

products.name: Capital-Back Endowment Plan
products.blurb: A savings contract that returns the sum assured at maturity, with survival benefits paid at intervals along the way.

products.name: Children’s Education Endowment
products.blurb: A fund built to a child’s university dates, with a waiver so the plan completes even if the paying parent dies.

products.name: Retirement Endowment with Profits
products.blurb: A with-profits endowment that converts to an annuity or pays a lump sum at the elected retirement date.

products.name: Five-Year Short Endowment
products.blurb: A five-year savings contract with a single or regular premium and a guaranteed maturity value.

products.name: Money-Back Endowment Plan
products.blurb: A proportion of the sum assured is paid at each survival interval, the balance with bonuses at maturity.

products.name: Unit-Linked Wealth Endowment
products.blurb: An endowment whose maturity value is the fund: units allocated at each dealing point, with a minimum death benefit guaranteed.

products.name: Takaful Education Savings Plan
products.blurb: A Shariah-compliant education fund built in the participant investment fund, with tabarru’ cover on the paying parent.

products.name: Standalone Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: A lump sum on first diagnosis of a condition on the filed schedule, independent of any life cover.

products.name: Comprehensive Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: The widest filed condition schedule, including major organ failure, stroke and coronary artery bypass.

products.name: Early-Stage Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: Pays a proportion of the sum assured at an early stage of a listed condition, and again at an advanced stage.

products.name: Multi-Pay Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: Pays once per condition group up to a stated number of claims, with a survival period between them.

products.name: Women’s Specific Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: Conditions specific to women, including the listed gynaecological cancers and complications of pregnancy.

products.name: Children’s Critical Illness Cover
products.blurb: A lump sum on a child’s diagnosis, with a parental accommodation benefit while the child is hospitalised.

products.name: Term Life with Critical Illness Bundle
products.blurb: Level term life with critical illness cover attached as a rider, priced as one contract and one premium.

products.name: Critical Illness Takaful
products.blurb: Wakalah-based critical illness cover out of the participant risk fund, with a Shariah-compliant condition schedule.

products.name: Lifestyle Income Protection
products.blurb: A monthly benefit after a deferred period when illness or injury stops the customer working, to a stated retirement age.

products.name: Lifestyle Loan Protection
products.blurb: Services a named personal loan while the customer cannot work, up to the outstanding balance and a monthly cap.

products.name: Lifestyle Protection Plan
products.blurb: One plan carrying death, critical illness and income replacement, so a household is covered on all three axes.

products.name: Lifestyle Wealth Plan (Unit-Linked)
products.blurb: A lifestyle plan whose savings leg is invested in units, with the protection leg charged per mille from the fund.

products.name: Lifestyle Takaful Plan
products.blurb: A wakalah family takaful plan combining savings in the participant investment fund with tabarru’ protection.

products.name: Mortgage Redemption Plan
products.blurb: A decreasing sum assured matched to the lender’s amortisation schedule, assigned to the bank at issue.

products.name: Mortgage Protection (Level)
products.blurb: A level sum assured over the mortgage term for a customer on an interest-only or bullet facility.

products.name: Mortgage Protection with Critical Illness
products.blurb: Mortgage protection that also clears the loan on a listed diagnosis, not only on death.

products.name: Mortgage Payment Protection
products.blurb: Pays the mortgage instalment for a limited number of months after involuntary unemployment, illness or accident.

products.name: Mortgage Takaful Plan
products.blurb: A decreasing takaful cover over a Shariah-compliant home finance facility, assigned to the financier.

products.name: Individual Inpatient Medical
products.blurb: Hospital admission, surgery and day-case treatment on the network, with a stated room category.

products.name: Outpatient & Inpatient Medical
products.blurb: Inpatient cover plus consultations, diagnostics and pharmacy on the outpatient side, subject to a co-pay.

products.name: Maternity & Newborn Cover
products.blurb: Antenatal care, delivery and newborn care, with a waiting period before the first claim is payable.

products.name: Dental & Optical Care Plan
products.blurb: Routine and major dental treatment plus optical correction, on an annual limit per discipline.

products.name: International Medical with Evacuation
products.blurb: Worldwide treatment including medical evacuation and repatriation, for a customer who travels or is posted abroad.

products.name: SME Group Medical Scheme
products.blurb: A staff medical scheme for a small employer, rated on the group’s age profile rather than individual evidence.

products.name: Corporate Group Medical Scheme
products.blurb: A large-group scheme with a network tier per employee grade, experience-rated at renewal.

products.name: Health Takaful Plan
products.blurb: A wakalah health plan with claims paid from the participant risk fund and surplus shared back under the filed gates.

products.name: Comprehensive Motor Cover
products.blurb: Own-damage and third-party cover for a private vehicle, with agency repair for the first years.

products.name: Third-Party Liability Motor
products.blurb: The statutory minimum: third-party bodily injury and property damage, with no own-damage cover.

products.name: Commercial Fleet Motor
products.blurb: A whole fleet on one policy and one renewal date, rated on the schedule of vehicles and the claims history.

products.name: Single-Trip Travel Cover
products.blurb: Emergency medical, repatriation, cancellation and baggage for one journey, from the day of departure.

products.name: Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
products.blurb: Unlimited trips inside a twelve-month period, each up to a stated number of days.

products.name: Schengen Visa Travel Cover
products.blurb: The minimum medical and repatriation limit a Schengen visa application requires, with the certificate issued at once.

products.name: Family Travel Cover
products.blurb: One policy for two adults and their dependent children travelling together, at a family rate.

products.name: Senior Traveller Cover
products.blurb: Travel cover for the over-65s with a declared-condition questionnaire and a higher medical limit.

products.name: Business Travel & Accident Cover
products.blurb: Corporate travel with accident benefits, equipment cover and a political-evacuation extension.

products.name: Travel Takaful Plan

note.title: Role access matrix
note.headline: Enable or disable any tab, section or sub-section — per role
note.body: This is the role-driven tree the console enforces: select a role, then switch each Tab, Section and Sub-Section between Full (visible and editable), Read-only (visible, not editable) and Hidden (not rendered in that role’s navigation). Children inherit from their parent until you override them, and changing a parent re-seats the whole branch so a hidden section can never leak a visible sub-section. These are roles — the policy office, the underwriter, the branch officer — not user logins. Named user accounts, credentials and login will reference a role id when the user-profile layer lands.

note.title: What's New

note.body: What's New is the filed record of what shipped: each entry names its source (commit, PR or change request) and says why it exists, what changed, and what you need to do, in that order. journey:allocation.body: The first allocation is executed against the published valuation: the premium net of charges buys units at the price for the dealing point that the instruction time fell into, and the result is compared with the signed target weights.

Compare the executed weights with the signed target weights.
Note whether a rebalance was requested at issue.
journey:allocation.watch: Crossing the cut-off changes the valuation date, not the amount. The explanation on each line says which rule applied.

master:products.title: Products
master:products.headline: The product factory: the whole shelf, editable as a table
master:products.body: Every variety this tenant may sell is on file with the numbers the engines read: entry ages, the base rate per 1,000, the income multiple, the automatic binding limit, the facultative threshold, the AI straight-through limit, the omni-channel name and the evidence bands. The shelf is a grid now: a cell is the field, **Copy line** starts a new variety as an exact twin of the row beside it, and saving files the batch in one audited bulk call — or you take the sample sheet away, fill in ninety rows and upload it back.
doThis: Filter by line or search an id, then edit the cell: the row in focus is the row the checklist above reads, so the two cannot disagree.
Copy a line, change the one thing that differs, save it — or use the server-side copy to bring the whole rating grid with the twin.
Read the refusal written into a red row: the good rows in the batch file anyway, and the reason names the cell.
master:products.watch: A row is a draft until it is saved, and an unsaved draft survives a reload. A minimum entry age at or above the maximum, a facultative threshold below the binding limit, or an AI limit above it is refused, and a product with no underwriting rules cannot be quoted — the factory registers both together.

master:product-rating.title: Product rating
master:product-rating.headline: The tariff: age band, gender, occupational rank and sum assured
master:product-rating.body: A product’s base rate is one number; a life is not one number. This is where the price is filed by band — premium per 1,000 of sum assured each year, and, for a unit-linked or takaful plan, the cost of insurance per 1,000 each policy month. Rows are matched on product, kind, gender, both ages, rank, sum band and scope, so uploading a band updates it instead of leaving two prices beside each other.
doThis: Pick the product and filter to mortality if you are reviewing the cost of insurance.
Copy a band, widen the ages or change the rate, and save the row — or download the sample sheet, fill it in and upload ninety rows at once.
Read the holes and the overlaps before you sign the tariff off: a life in an uncovered band cannot be quoted, only referred.
master:product-rating.watch: Rates are decimal money per 1,000, never a percentage: the engine divides by the currency’s scale and rounds once, so 2.75 and 2.7500 are the same tariff and 2,75 is not.

master:omni-channel.title: Omni channel
master:omni-channel.headline: Every route the plan is sold through, and what each partner is paid
master:omni-channel.body: Channels first, then the partners on them, then the terms each partner holds for each product: which plans are on its shelf, what the plan is called there, whether its rates differ from the filed tariff, and the commission and clawback schedules behind the sale. None of it exists until it is set up, and an unset-up omni-channel is why a distribution manager ends up with prices in a spreadsheet.
doThis: If the six standard channels are not filed yet, press the button — it creates the routes and nothing else.
File a partner against one channel, then put products on its shelf; the terms grid follows the shelf.
Keep commission schedules inside the ceiling on the channel, and say which period a clawback counts in.
master:omni-channel.watch: A partner cannot be paid more than its channel’s ceiling, a channel with partners on it cannot be deleted, and the clawback here is the master record only — the money a period actually owes is settled by the ERP’s commission ledger, which this screen cannot reach.

email:accounts.title: Accounts
email:accounts.headline: The mailboxes, and the settings their credentials live in
email:accounts.body: Each account has one address, a display name, a reply-to, a department, a transport kind and a daily limit. Credential settings are named — GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, SMTP_PASSWORD — and their values stay in the environment. Several accounts may share a department; one address may belong to only one account.
doThis: File the sending address and the department that owns it.
Name the environment settings the transport needs; never type a secret into this screen.
Disable an account rather than deleting it if events still point at it, or reassign those events first.
email:accounts.watch: Removing an account that events still use is refused. A disabled account shows as a blocker on each of its events, which is deliberate: silence is how a customer letter goes missing.

email:event-routes.title: Event routes
email:event-routes.headline: One business event, one sender, one set of words
email:event-routes.body: Every event — quotation, policy issuance, information pack, renewal request, alteration, receipt, claim acknowledgement, claim settlement, reinsurance placement, welcome pack, lapse, surrender, complaint and fund statement — carries its own sending account, recipients, copy, subject, body, attachments and a service level. Templates use a closed list of placeholders, so a typo is refused at filing rather than printed as a blank.
doThis: Pick the account that owns the event, then check the recipient and copy lists.
Write the subject and body with the placeholders from the list; a queue:<department> recipient resolves to that department’s enabled mailbox.
Set a service-level in hours where the letter promises an answer, and preview the rendered result before saving is trusted.
email:event-routes.watch: An unknown or unclosed placeholder is a refusal. The route can be disabled without deleting it, and a blocked route is shown as blocked on the event.

master:providers.title: Providers
master:providers.headline: Who carries the risk, where they are licensed, and who reinsures them
master:providers.body: An insurance provider is filed with its home country, home regulator, home licence and which books it may write. In every country it sells in, it needs a branch registered against that country’s requirements, the country’s own currency, local premium management and an investment held where the quotation was generated — and a separate reinsurance arrangement for that country, with retakaful where the business is Takaful. The home licence is not a licence to write abroad.
doThis: File the provider, then register its branch in each selling country with the registration number and regulator that country gave it.
File the country reinsurance arrangement: reinsurer, kind, basis, cession, retention, limit and the regulatory reference.
Attach the products the provider underwrites in each country, in that country’s currency. Press the worked-example button to see the Marsh pattern in one go.
master:providers.watch: A branch that is applied for, suspended or withdrawn stops the sale. A product master in another currency is refused rather than relabelled, and a Takaful product needs retakaful, not the group’s conventional treaty.

master:provider-selling.title: Provider selling
master:provider-selling.headline: Conventional and Takaful are two checkboxes, narrowed down the route
master:provider-selling.body: The channel, the sub-channel and the partner each carry a Conventional and a Takaful checkbox. The effective permission is the intersection: a broker that sells both cannot widen an agency desk that has been narrowed to Conventional only. The same screen files the channel’s presence in each country — its local licence, operating name, currency and appointed providers — and probes a sale before anyone quotes it.
doThis: Tick the boxes at the scope that actually decides: the channel for the whole route, the sub-channel for a desk, the partner for one entity.
File the country presence with the country’s currency and the appointed providers.
Run the sellability probe with provider, country, channel, sub-channel and partner: every refusal names the missing filing, not just “not allowed”.
master:provider-selling.watch: A sale is priced in the country’s currency, premium is managed by the local branch and the investment stays in the country where the quotation was generated. The provider’s home country is recorded for capital reporting, not as the place the customer’s money sits.

role-matrix:access-tree.title: Access tree
role-matrix:access-tree.headline: The Tab → Section → Sub-Section switchboard
role-matrix:access-tree.body: Each tab is a branch; its sections are nodes under it and each section has its own sub-sections. Full means visible and editable, Read means visible but locked, Hidden means the node is not shown at all. A node without an explicit override shows "inherit" and follows its parent. Changing a tab clears child overrides so the whole branch moves together; granting a child afterwards creates one deliberate exception.

role-matrix:doa-limits.body: A DOA cap is a decimal money limit with a currency. Supervisor- and manager-tier roles may change caps for lower-tier roles, but never above their own cap; Administration may set any finite cap and holds unlimited authority itself. An officer-tier role cannot edit a cap or this tree — it raises a tracked limit-increase request, routed through the Entity × Channel × Sub-Channel supervisor chain, and the approving supervisor/manager is what applies the new cap.

As an officer, use the request form: state the requested cap and the operational reason, then follow the tracked request in the approver inbox.

role-matrix:doa-limits.watch: Self-approval is refused, an approver above their own cap auto-escalates, and an officer can never grant itself a higher limit by calling the API directly.

datasets.label: Policy issuance fact
datasets.grain: One row per active, lapsed or ended policy known to the ERP
datasets.lineage: ErpManager policy snapshot; linked to party and product masters by party_id and product_id.

datasets.label: Premium receipt fact
datasets.grain: One row per posted premium receipt; amount and fee use the receipt currency
datasets.lineage: ErpManager.receivePremium → unit-linked, takaful or billing register; journal_ids point to posted ledger journals.

datasets.label: Fund NAV fact
datasets.grain: One row per fund per published valuation date
datasets.source: NavEngine.valuationHistory + fund composition and charge schedule
datasets.lineage: NavEngine.publishValuation; reproduce from valuation date, unit count, published price and residual. NAV = units × price + residual.

datasets.label: Claim fact
datasets.grain: One row per claim, including reserve, approval, settlement and recovery amounts
datasets.source: ClaimsEngine claims + approval authority + recovery register
datasets.lineage: ClaimsEngine.register/triage/reserve/approve/settle/recover; amount facts are in the claim functional currency and tie to claim journals.

datasets.label: Reinsurance utilisation fact
datasets.grain: One row per treaty and book at the warehouse as-of date
datasets.lineage: Treaty cessions and recoveries in the conventional and retakaful books; utilisation ties to the treaties and ledger journals.

datasets.label: Distribution commission schedule fact
datasets.grain: One row per partner × product × policy-year contract term (not an earned commission transaction)
datasets.lineage: Filed distribution contract terms. Earned commission cash events require a receipt with partner attribution; terms are not presented as paid amounts.

datasets.label: Super member policy fact
datasets.grain: One row per super member policy with balance, contribution, charge and income totals
datasets.lineage: SuperFundsRegistry.createMemberPolicy/contribute/runMonthlyCharges/allocateIncome; every adjustment has a matching funds-accounting voucher.

datasets.label: Funds-accounting voucher line fact
datasets.grain: One row per debit or credit voucher line, with policy, product, partner, channel, sub-channel and resolved GL account
datasets.lineage: Voucher event → mapping resolution → balanced DR/CR lines; ledger_journal_id links each posted voucher to the double-entry ledger.

datasets.label: Super member balance snapshot
datasets.grain: One row per member policy at the warehouse cut-off date
datasets.source: SuperFundsRegistry member units, NAV, balance and charge register
datasets.lineage: Units × NAV per unit is the investment value; member_balance_minor is the liability to the member, with total charges in the same currency.

dataBreachAgreement.terms: By accepting, the connecting party agrees: (1) warehouse data is received PII-masked only and re-identification is prohibited; (2) any suspected breach is notified to the insurer security desk within 24 hours and the connection is suspended until cleared; (3) masked extracts are never joined across transactions to re-identify a person (masking rotates per transaction by design); (4) secrets live in the deployment secret store, are rotated at least every 90 days, and are never pasted into tickets, chats or commits; (5) on termination all extracts are deleted and deletion is certified in writing.

masking.algorithm: SHA-256 keyed hash with per-transaction derived salt (one-way, no decode path)
masking.piiColumns: party/member/employer identifiers, names, email, phone, national IDs and secrets
masking.note: Masking is one-way (SHA-256 keyed hash, per-transaction derived salt). The method rotates on every transaction, salts are never exported, and there is no decode/unmask path in the codebase.
